sections.html:
Walton County lies in the Piedmont, roughly 30 miles from downtown Atlanta, and its growth shows the spread of metro Atlanta. Residents numbered 83,768 in 2010 and 96,673 in 2020, and the July 2025 estimate is 112,696, which is 16.6% above the 2020 count. Monroe holds the courthouse and is the biggest city, with Loganville the other major one. Social Circle, Between and Good Hope also sit within the borders.

The Walton County School District serves everything except Social Circle, which runs its own city district. The county and the school system each levy their own share, so the district matters when you read a bill. A six-member commission elected by district, plus a chairman chosen countywide, sets the county's share.

Homeownership here is high and values sit just above the U.S. median. For 2020 to 2024 the owner-occupied home median is $339,500, compared with $332,700 for the country.

  • 79.3% of housing units are owner-occupied, against 65.2% across the U.S.
  • Monthly gross rent has a median of $1,175.
  • Median household income is $84,945 across 35,755 households.
  • The county had 39,911 housing units on July 1, 2025, and issued 569 building permits during 2025.

With so much new building going up, an older house with deferred repairs or a tax balance is easier to sell to a buyer who accepts it as it stands. A listing may be a lot in Monroe or acreage out in the rural parts, and buyers of either will want to see the current bill before they make an offer.

sections.h2: Where to send questions and payments
sections.html:
The Tax Commissioner issues one statement per parcel. For Monroe owners it also carries the city's share, because Monroe stopped mailing its own bills in 2016 and now relies on the county statement and its date. Delinquent city bills from 2015 and earlier are still paid at Monroe City Hall.

  • Main counter: 303 S. Hammond Drive, Suite 100, Monroe, GA 30655; weekdays 8:30 a.m. to 4:45 p.m.
  • Property tax line (770) 266-1736, email WCTC@co.walton.ga.us.
  • Tax Assessors, same building: (770) 267-1352.
  • Search and pay: tax.waltoncountypay.com.

Tag renewals have their own window in the courthouse at 303 South Hammond Drive, (770) 267-1335. Homeowners with a mortgage should know that the mailed copy goes only to the homeowner, so lenders often pull the bill from a third-party service.

The county mails the bill to the owner on record for January 1 only, so a lender or a newly arrived owner should obtain a copy rather than wait. Churches, nonprofit hospitals and public property can be exempt once the assessors approve, with the request due April 1.

Bills are mailed in late August, and November 15 is the due date. Late bills move through the steps below, in this order.

Walton County delinquency steps
WhenCharge or action
After November 15Interest on the unpaid portion, added monthly
At 90 days lateFi.Fa. lien fee: $20.50 under $100, $30.50 over $100
Every 120 days5% penalty on what remains, capped at 20%
Before a lien30-day notice of intent

A Fi.Fa. goes on the General Execution Docket kept by the Clerk of Superior Court and lasts seven years, and it may show up on credit reports. The office takes partial payments, but charges continue on the leftover amount. A tax sale, when one is scheduled, is an auction outside the Walton County Government Building on a first Tuesday, advertised in the Walton Tribune for four straight Wednesdays.

Real property returns and homestead applications are due January 1 through April 1 at the Tax Assessors' Office. A required return that is never filed draws a 10% penalty on the value left off, and personal property returns are due every year with the same penalty for late filing.

You can contest the assessment within 45 days of the notice's mailing date. The assessors respond first, and the file then goes to the Board of Equalization automatically. Mobile and modular homes get two chances to contest, during the return period and within 45 days of a bill that usually arrives in January.

  • Owners 65 and older are exempt from Walton County School District tax on the house and one acre.
  • Owners 70 and older receive up to $30,000 off on land beyond one acre.
  • A filed PT-61 transfer form can serve as a return if the property was not changed.
  • A refund claim for tax paid in error goes in writing to the board of commissioners within three years, and it must rest on an error, not a value disagreement.

Ask the Tax Assessors' Office to confirm an exemption is on file before you list, since failing to apply by the deadline costs the exemption for that year.

Email the settlement statement to WCTC@co.walton.ga.us or fax it to (770) 267-1416 right after closing. The office can mail a duplicate bill to the buyer when the purchase happened before November 15 of that tax year.

Before you close, get a payoff figure dated for the closing day, because monthly interest keeps changing it. If a Fi.Fa. is already recorded, paying the tax, fees, penalties and interest cancels it. The commissioner does not sell liens in bulk to outside investors.

Anyone who sold after January 1 should keep the closing statement handy for the commissioner's records, as the January 1 owner still receives the first bill.

An inherited house, a rental or a place with several years behind can close without repair demands when the buyer purchases as-is and the title company settles the county first. A short order of work helps: request the payoff, confirm exemptions with the assessors, hand both to the title company, and send the settlement statement to the commissioner once the deed is recorded.

Collect the parcel number, a copy of your deed, and the most recent assessment notice before you call either office. Those three items answer most questions at the counter. If your family has held the house for years, ask the tax line about every open year and whether any Fi.Fa. sits on the docket, since a surprise lien found at the title stage can push back a closing date. Owners who live out of town can handle most of this by phone or email, and the online search shows the current balance. Keep a note of who you spoke with, and ask for any payoff figure by email so you have it in writing when the title company asks.

faqs.q: What day are Walton County real estate bills due?
faqs.a: November 15. The county mails statements in late August, and balances left after the due date begin accruing interest.

faqs.q: Which Walton County office handles exemptions?
faqs.a: The Tax Assessors' Office at 303 S. Hammond Drive, phone (770) 267-1352. April 1 is the usual cutoff for applications.

faqs.q: Does Monroe mail a separate city tax bill?
faqs.a: No. Since 2016 Walton County sends a single consolidated statement that includes Monroe city tax, and it is due on the county's date.

faqs.q: What happens 90 days after the Walton County due date?
faqs.a: A Fi.Fa. lien fee applies, $20.50 on bills under $100 and $30.50 on larger bills, after a 30-day notice. A 5% penalty is added every 120 days up to 20%.

faqs.q: Can a house with a Walton County Fi.Fa. be sold?
faqs.a: Yes. Paying the tax with its fees, penalties and interest cancels the lien, and the closing agent can do that from your proceeds using a current written payoff.
